IV. 2. 104</ls>; <ls>Vārt.</ls>] .²1 .³({%a%}) Continual, perpetual, constant, everlasting, eternal, uninterrupted; यथा त्वमसि दुर्धर्षो धर्मनित्यः प्रजाहितः <ls>Rām. 7. 37. 8</ls>; यदि नित्यमनित्येन लभ्यते <ls>H. 1. 48</ls>; नित्यज्योत्स्नाः प्रतिहततमोवृत्तिरम्याः प्रदोषाः <ls>Me.</ls> (regarded by <ls>Malli.</ls> as an interpolation); <ls>Ms. 2. 206</ls>. .³({%b%}) Imperishable, indestructible; पृथिवी द्विविधा नित्याऽनित्या च <ls>Tarka K.</ls> .²2 Invariable, regular, fixed, not optional, regularly prescribed (<ab>opp.</ab> काम्य). .²3 Necessary, obligatory, essential. .²4 Ordinary, usual (<ab>opp.</ab> नौमित्तिक). .²5 (At the end of <ab>comp.</ab>) Constantly dwelling in, perpetually engaged in or busy with; जाह्नवीतीर˚, अरण्य˚, आदान˚, ध्यान˚ <ab>&c.</ab> .{@-त्यः@} The ocean. .{@-त्या@} .²1 An epithet of the goddess Durgā. .²2 A plough-share. .{@-त्यम्@} An indispensable or inevitable act. .{@-त्यम्@} {%ind.%} Daily, constantly, always, ever, perpetually, eternally.
